audit_question.trigger_rationale: The new source resolves the reset question adversely to the proposed protection: recover preserves existing bookkeeping and makeBallot resets no counters. Ballot selection also permits equality with its bounds. These observations strengthen the discriminator but require inventory correction and initialization evidence before a terminal judgment.

input.selection_rationale: Continue F3 consumption. The acquired helpers establish that serialization and fresh proposal allocation do not by themselves protect existing-instance recovery: recovery retains bookkeeping, and ballot generation neither clears counts nor guarantees a strictly newer ballot. The retry call also supplies a ballot where an instance index is expected. These are observed implementation facts, not proof of a legal unsupported commitment. Correct the affected descriptive responsibilities and acquire the exact initialization declarations before deriving a normative obligation.

descriptive_issues.reason: The inventory leaves ballot generation and recovery bookkeeping unresolved and references B9 without supplying its behavior. recover preserves existing bookkeeping; makeBallot changes lastTriedBallot without resetting counters, and uses non-strict bounds when selecting a ballot. handleAcceptReply passes areply.Ballot to this instance-indexed helper, whereas prepare retry and recover pass an instance index. Represent these distinct paths and their affected instance ownership before reassessing F3 consumption; they directly change the delayed-report discriminator.
